headline: Strict Backcountry Lotteries for Sandstone Entry
reservation: Access to Coyote Buttes North (The Wave) and South requires a permit obtained through a competitive online lottery months in advance or a geofence-based daily lottery via the BLM. General monument entry is open, but overnight wilderness camping requires separate authorization. Systems are managed by the Bureau of Land Management and are subject to change; verify at the official BLM site.

days.title: House Rock Valley and Condor Vistas

stops.name: California Condor Viewing Area
stops.detail: Scan the limestone cliffs for reintroduced raptors; best viewed with binoculars from the designated pullout on House Rock Valley Road.

stops.name: Navajo Bridge
stops.detail: Walk the historic pedestrian span over the Colorado River to view the sheer walls of Marble Canyon.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours total driving; conditions vary significantly on unpaved valley roads.
days.note: Avoid House Rock Valley Road during or immediately after rain due to impassable clay mud.

days.title: Deep Sand and Sculpted Stone

stops.name: White Pocket
stops.detail: Explore the brain-like cauliflower rock formations; requires extreme high-clearance 4WD for deep sand navigation.

stops.name: Buckskin Gulch
stops.detail: Hike into one of the world's longest slot canyons, observing the undulating patterns carved by ancient floods.

days.driving: Allow 5+ hours for off-road navigation; travel is slow and requires specialized vehicle skills.
days.note: Check flash flood warnings religiously before entering any slot canyon.

days.title: Monument Horizons and High Desert History

stops.name: Big Water Visitor Center
stops.detail: Examine paleontological exhibits detailing the dinosaur tracks and prehistoric life of the Grand Staircase region.

stops.name: Lees Ferry
stops.detail: Visit the historic river crossing and launch point for Grand Canyon expeditions at the monument's southern edge.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours; primarily paved routes with gravel access to the ferry area.
days.note: Winter travelers should prepare for short daylight hours and plummeting evening temperatures.

intel.title: Unpaved Route Stability
intel.text: The primary artery, House Rock Valley Road, is dirt and becomes dangerously slick when wet. Always verify road status at the Paria Contact Station before leaving pavement.

intel.title: Remote Border Supplies
intel.text: There are no services within the monument boundaries. Top off tanks in Kanab or Page before entering the House Rock Valley corridor.

intel.title: Wilderness Dead Zones
intel.text: Cellular service is non-existent in the canyons and most of the plateau. Download offline maps and carry a satellite communication device for emergencies.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Wire Pass and White Pocket have limited dirt parking areas. Arrive early during spring and fall peaks to secure a spot without blocking access roads.

intel.title: Permit Windows
intel.text: The online lottery for The Wave occurs four months in advance. The daily lottery requires being within the geofence near Kanab or Page during the application window.

plan.arrival: Pick up 4WD rental at Page Municipal Airport (PGA). Stock up on several gallons of water and food in Page before the 70-minute drive to the monument gate.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is essential for White Pocket and Coyote Buttes South; check rental contracts for off-road exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: White Pocket offers dramatic textures at sunset, though shadows deepen quickly in the surrounding basins.
